attempts.rationale: Ranking is unstable and several models are correlated; use a robust weighted scheme with inverse error to give more weight to better performers while still mixing.
The series shows strong seasonality and unstable ranking; a robust median combination might reduce influence of outliers.
The series has strong seasonality and unstable ranking; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of outlier models while still using many models.
Try a DBA combination on the full pool to test a different robust algorithm given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
Test a per-horizon weighted combination using softmax_neg_error to see if it improves over the robust DBA, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
Test a simple mean combination on the full pool to see if averaging outlier effects improves over weighted schemes given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
I will test a per‑horizon weighted combination to see if the best model changes across the 8‑step horizon; the series has strong seasonality and unstable ranking.
Test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k mean handle (w5) to see if focusing on the best few models per step improves over the global best‑per‑horizon w4.
The series has strong seasonality and unstable ranking, so a robust trimmed mean with a smaller trim may reduce influence of a few bad models without over‑shrinking.
Try a robust DBA combination on the smaller, more stable pool5 to see if it improves over the mean of pool5.
try a per‑horizon weighted combo on the small, stable pool5 to capture horizon‑specific strengths (ranking unstable, strong seasonality).

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool5 weighted by w7' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8326. Series context: trend strength 0.9567 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.158); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.44.
